newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS says more competition could impact '97.
newsitem.headline: SAS says more competition could impact '97.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines Systems (SAS) posted a 31 percent fall in pre-tax profits in 1996, saying stronger competition could further hit revenues in 1997.
"Competition in the airline industry is expected...to intensify further in 1997 which could lead to big over capacity putting pressure on prices and revenue," SAS said in a statement.

SAS reported a pre-tax profit of 1.82 billion crowns for the year to December 31, slightly above a company forecast of 1.74 billion crowns made in mid-November and above an average market forecast of 1.72 billion crowns.
SAS said it was working on certain areas to try to avoid its performance deteriorating in 1997.
It estimated there would be a five to seven percent lift in the market where SAS operates during 1997.
The airline, owned by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and private investors, has vowed to counteract increased competition by cutting costs, lowering fares and improving service.
In 1996 eight new airlines started flying in SAS's market.
Group turnover dipped to 35.19 billion crowns from 35.40 billion crowns.
SAS was last week named among a group of nine airlines said by industry sources to be forming an alliance to counteract the proposed link-up between British Airways and American Airlines.
